Game plan

Generate repeated Choose One cards with Gem RatTier 3 and related effects, then let Turbo HogriderTier 6 convert those casts into Blood-Gem scaling. Jailbird JuggernautTier 5 is the source's primary Rally carry, while Thorned TrailblazerTier 4 adds more Choose One value.

FelboarTier 5 can consume shop stats in the demonstrated line, but the comp's identity is Hogrider plus Choose One volume—not generic Demon consumption.

How to build it

  • Bridge: collect Choose One generation without sacrificing basic board strength.
  • Commit: the source calls Turbo Hogrider the scaler; without it, the package lacks a reliable ceiling.
  • Scale: cast Choose One effects in the order that maximizes Gem production before moving stats.
  • Finish: transfer accumulated Blood Gems into resilient final carries and keep Juggernaut positioned to Rally safely.

Practical cautions

Do not spread permanent Gems across units you expect to sell. Delay transfers until the final carries are clear, but do not die holding a hand full of theoretical value.

The source's blunt warning is useful: miss Turbo Hogrider and this can become a very efficient route to eighth place. Treat the card as the commitment signal, not a hoped-for future miracle.

The late Tavern proof is much stronger than the earlier transition board: the source finishes with carries at 1.5k/2.2k, 1.9k/2.8k, and 2.4k/3.6k before winning. That is the payoff standard—not merely assembling the named pieces.

Experimental model v1

Quantitative evaluation

Observed source boards, a reproducible shop model, and external archetype benchmarks. These are separate signals—not one suspiciously magical tier letter.

  • Build windowMidgame engine; late only with fuel
  • Setup debtMedium — Choose One generation must already exist
  • ExecutionMedium — repeated casts, not full APM

Observed board trajectory

Recorded source games validate the growth calculation and achievable board. They are successful examples, not median outcomes.

End · Turn 14 18,120 total stats ≈ 7,470 attack · 10,650 health 6 bodies 100+ · 5 bodies 500+ · 3 bodies 1k+ 2.04× raw stats per turn over the previous 4 turns

Baseline calibration

The baseline is deliberately boring: ordinary core cards, legal board space, and no hero, trinket, Golden, or Discover miracle unless listed. It is compared with the source trajectory rather than bent until the high-roll magically becomes “average.”

Single-engine core floor +90 projected stats Turn 10 → 14 · projected end 1,133 Gem Day upgrades one Blood Gem stat, then each Hogrider plays that Gem on every other Quilboar.
Real source comparison +17,077 observed stats Observed end 18,120 · 189.74× the core-only gain Core floor accounts for 0.5% of the demonstrated growth.
  • One ordinary Turbo Hogrider and one Gem Rat
  • One Gem Day played each turn, alternating Attack and Health upgrades
  • Five other Quilboar receive each Hogrider Blood Gem
  • No Golden core, trinket, Discover chain, or additional Choose One generation

The demonstrated board is a high-roll ceiling trajectory. The named core alone does not reproduce it; extra Choose One volume, additional Hogriders, upgraded Gems, and secondary engines are material requirements.

How much luck?

Hard-roll v1 starts each modeled turn with 10 Gold, buys missing core cards immediately, and spends the rest refreshing at Tavern 6. It averages all eligible five-tribe lobbies and excludes Discovers, triples, heroes, trinkets, selling economy, and survival.

From scratch at Tavern 6 20.3% in eligible lobbies Common · about 1 in 4.9 eligible games 10.2% across all lobbies · about 1 in 9.8 games Need: Gem Rat, Turbo Hogrider
Gem Rat already owned 41.2% in eligible lobbies Common · about 1 in 2.4 eligible games 20.6% across all lobbies · about 1 in 4.9 games Need: Gem Rat, Turbo Hogrider · already own: Gem Rat
Gem Rat owned; one rival holds Hogrider 36.8% in eligible lobbies Common · about 1 in 2.7 eligible games 18.4% across all lobbies · about 1 in 5.4 games Need: Gem Rat, Turbo Hogrider · already own: Gem Rat

50,000 deterministic-seed simulations per scenario across 2 recruit turns. Pool-copy assumptions follow the Hearthstone Wiki Battlegrounds table captured 2026-08-09. This measures the shop hit from the stated position—not how often a player chooses, survives, or completes the high-roll ending.
